# tinyland-cleanup

> A conservative, cross-platform disk-pressure cleanup daemon for developer
> machines and CI hosts. It reclaims build-system and developer-tool caches on
> graduated levels (warning to critical), driven by whichever is worse — disk
> bytes or filesystem inodes — with dry-run review, per-plugin cooldown, and a
> stable JSON report. Conservative by default; disruptive actions are opt-in.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): overview, quick start, run modes
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): repository authority, safety defaults, agent operating notes
- [Usage](docs/usage.md): run modes, daemon lifecycle, reports, exit codes
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): config keys and Home Manager options

## Machine surfaces

- [JSON report schema](docs/json-report-schema.md): the `cycleReport` object from `--output json`
- [Plugins](docs/plugins.md): stable plugin names and what each cleans
- `main.go`: CLI flags and the `cycleReport`/`mountReport`/`pluginCycleReport` structs
- `config/default.yaml`: documented config schema; `config/config.go`: the typed schema

## Operating the daemon

- Modes: `--once --dry-run` (review), `--once` (clean once), `--daemon` (poll + cooldown).
- Force a level: `--level {warning,moderate,aggressive,critical}`.
- Constrain plugins: `--plugins bazel,nix`; list them: `--list-plugins --output json`.
- Effectiveness signal: `host_free_delta_bytes` and `host_inodes_free_delta` in the JSON report.
- Exit codes: `0` success, `1` runtime error, `2` config/flag error.
- Example: `tinyland-cleanup --once --dry-run --level critical --output json | jq '.plugins[] | {name, skip_reason, estimated_bytes_freed}'`
